title: Exclude the actual negative E ordinary decoder from width 296 with an error floor
body:
This source-bound application lowers the ordinary-decoder exclusion threshold for the actual 73-axis negative E endpoint from width 4198 to 296. For every width at least 296, every allowed ordinary endpoint has worst-case operator error at least `1541/1255956` in the fixed source chart. The complete kappa calculation is unchanged.

[Proof and scope](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b2ed5c35222665ceec0ab56c6937288f29635464/research/negative-e-decoder-gram-bound/README.md), [exact checks](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b2ed5c35222665ceec0ab56c6937288f29635464/research/negative-e-decoder-gram-bound/verify.py), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b2ed5c35222665ceec0ab56c6937288f29635464/research/negative-e-decoder-gram-bound/SOURCES.json), [registered replay](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b2ed5c35222665ceec0ab56c6937288f29635464/research/negative-e-decoder-gram-bound/VERIFY.json). Base: canonical main `32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04`, priority revision 7. Contribution head: `b2ed5c35222665ceec0ab56c6937288f29635464`.

The decoder observes the emitted negative bank and independent workspace. Ordinary address maps are columnwise monomial Cliffords; scalar mixing, instruction count and coefficients may depend on width. The source expansion has a unique nonmonomial Clifford path with fixed scalar coefficient `1541/418652`. The pointwise Gram bound makes that coefficient impossible to cancel with the ordinary span. Correlated original-input histories, paid calls, cross-column operations and nonlinear rounding are outside this claim.

CPython 3.12.14 warning-strict registered normal and optimized checks pass. Three immutable source copies match their Git objects and SHA256 pins. Independent checks recompute the spectral/path coefficient, 147 sparse native columns, four Clifford generator identities, 36 finite rational Gram bounds and complete geometric tails; nine controls cover source changes, an unproved width, projective phases and scalar placement. Both modes print `PASS_NEGATIVE_E_DECODER_GRAM_BOUND`; the launcher prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/negative-e-decoder-gram-bound
```

Python 3.12 and the standard library suffice. Committed-byte checks pass. The complete owner-path separation and general Clifford counting theorem are credited written premises, not newly audited theorems. Their full scientific suites, independent human/proof-kernel review, selected cold replay, physical emission, precision application and complete invoice were not run here. The norm floor is stated in the original endpoint chart and is not a paid-child lower bound. No smaller-width optimality or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. Hosted status is unconfirmed at publication.

Credit JoyboyBrian (@JoyboyBrian) for [PR #5508](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5508), its [pinned actual decoder/path proof](https://github.com/JoyboyBrian/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7e6824d560337e2b2e49da8b98727183491f6ecf/research/odd-e8-negative-exit-algebra/PROOF.md) and [exact source result](https://github.com/JoyboyBrian/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7e6824d560337e2b2e49da8b98727183491f6ecf/research/odd-e8-negative-exit-algebra/RESULT.json). Credit Ali Romman (@aliromman) for [PR #5526](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5526) and its [pinned pointwise Clifford Gram theorem](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32e014bec9206f3987857e6153ec0fd8058f04e3/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/PROOF.md). Both sources retain their native, fresh-stage, stabilizer and compiler lineage. The [scoped claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19174457) reserves only this application.

Next: bind a changed paid decoder or correlated-history contract to its complete original-input identity and added-paid/lost-target ledger. Those interfaces may evade this obstruction, but all physical costs remain payable.

Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.
